learning_outcomes.text: Fluently handle electrical terminology, symbology, magnitudes, and units
Understand and model the basic elements that constitute an electrical circuit
Master general circuit analysis techniques: nodes and meshes
Simplify circuits using element associations and Thévenin and Norton equivalents
Perform power and energy analysis in electrical circuits
Analyze the transient behavior of electrical circuits
Apply node or mesh analysis to circuits in sinusoidal steady-state
Perform power balances in sinusoidal steady-state
Evaluate the effect of frequency in sinusoidal steady-state
Analyze circuits with magnetically coupled coils and transformers
Understand the capabilities of electrical circuit simulation software tools

assessment_rules: There are two evaluation options: continuous evaluation or final evaluation. For continuous evaluation, the final grade is a weighted average of three partial exams (90% total) and a practical exam (10%). Approved partial exams eliminate that material from the final exam. For final evaluation, the final grade is a weighted average of a single final exam (90%) covering all material and a practical exam (10%). Both theoretical exams (partial and final) are paper-based problem-solving tests, while the practical exam is computer-based using software taught in class. Programmable calculators are allowed.
